label: Revision-authored AQA-style practice question (original, not an AQA question)

question.context: Revision-authored AQA-style practice. A growing private biotechnology business needs £450,000. Its founders value experienced investors who can provide specialist advice but wish to understand the effect on control.
question.stem: Which comparison of venture capital and equity crowdfunding is most defensible?

options.label: A
options.text: Venture capital always leaves founders with complete control; equity crowdfunding always requires fixed interest repayments.

options.label: B
options.text: Both always involve loans rather than ownership, and neither can dilute the founders.

options.label: C
options.text: Venture capital may offer expertise and a concentrated investor relationship, while either equity route can dilute ownership and investor expectations must be considered.

options.label: D
options.text: Crowdfunding is automatically free capital and never carries marketing, reporting or compliance costs.

option_rationale: A is incorrect because equity investment can dilute founder ownership; equity crowdfunding is not necessarily debt.
B is incorrect because both venture capital and equity crowdfunding may involve selling equity.
C is correct because venture capital can bring experience alongside finance, but equity funding may dilute control; the terms matter.
D is incorrect because crowdfunding can involve platform fees, investor reporting and equity dilution.
mark_scheme.model_answer: C. Choose finance by the business's goals, ownership/control implications, cost and non-financial support; neither route is universally better.
